scope: descriptive mapping of terminal G2 v0.5 paired trajectories to manuscript language; no endpoint, estimand, stopping rule, or inferential test is changed

outcome_access_attestation.reason: the original protocol froze metrics and within-world reporting but did not operationalize its qualitative narrative branches

branch_precedence.rule: either selected world has fewer than three completed pairs
branch_precedence.manuscript_language: Right-censoring left insufficient paired coverage for a qualitative repeatability classification; all available pairs are reported without substitution.

branch_precedence.rule: at least three of four core trajectory metrics are directionally consistent in both worlds and have opposite signs between worlds
branch_precedence.manuscript_language: Fresh trajectories reproduced predominantly opposite, world-conditioned responses to nominal material information across the core lifecycle metrics.

branch_precedence.rule: at least four of the eight world-by-core-metric classifications are mixed
branch_precedence.manuscript_language: Fresh trajectories frequently reversed sign within a fixed physical world, indicating that provider-trajectory variability dominated any stable material-information pattern.
Repeatability was metric-specific or non-opposing across worlds; endpoint and lifecycle effects are therefore reported as a profile rather than a single prior-information effect.

claim_boundaries: classification is descriptive and does not create a population-level material-information effect
raw nominal-minus-opaque signs are reported; lower values are favorable for discovery fraction and drawdown but the branch rule concerns repeatability, not benefit
all pair rows and per-world summaries remain authoritative over the qualitative branch label
the mapping supplement was frozen after execution began and must not be described as preregistered before the first provider call
